claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you're looking to claim for Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now, could you please tell me if you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit (currently £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child) towards looking after him — for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to make sure everything is in order:

Is anyone else currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one more question:

Is Alex currently in hospital, residential care, or local authority care? Or is he living at home with you under normal circumstances?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, he's been in hospital for a while now - about a couple of months or so.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex's hospital stay. I hope he recovers well soon.

Since Alex has been in hospital for around 2 months, I need to clarify a couple of things:

1. Has Alex been in hospital continuously for more than 12 weeks, or is it less than that?

2. During his hospital stay, are you regularly spending money on him (for example, on items like clothes, toys, treats, or other things for his benefit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been just under 12 weeks - about 11 weeks now. And yes, I've been regularly spending money on him - buying him clothes, magazines, his favorite snacks, things like that to keep his spirits up.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing those details. It sounds like you're doing a wonderful job supporting Alex during his hospital stay.

That's very helpful information. Based on what you've told me:

- Alex has been in hospital for about 11 weeks, which is under the 12-week limit
- You are regularly spending money on him during his stay

One final question: Is Alex in a hospital in the UK, or is he in hospital abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's in a hospital here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex is under 16 years old
- ✅ You are responsible for Alex (he normally lives with you)
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- ✅ Although Alex has been in hospital for about 11 weeks, this is within the 12-week limit

**Important to note:** If Alex's hospital stay extends beyond 12 weeks, you should inform HMRC. However, because you are regularly spending money on Alex during his stay (clothes, magazines, snacks, etc.), you may still be able to continue receiving Child Benefit even after the 12-week point. This is an exception that applies to children in UK hospitals when the parent regularly spends money on them.

I hope Alex gets well soon. If you have any other questions about Child Benefit, please don't hesitate to ask!
